Propose the validation rules for the columns above (and for whole records where useful). Return JSON only.

rules.condition: The same complete record (id, beer_name, brewery, ounces, abv, ibu, style, location) must not appear more than once.
rules.reason: Each record is one beer listing with its own id. An exact duplicate points to a double load or ingestion error.

rules.condition: Serving size must be a number followed by an ounce unit (oz, oz., ounce, ounces), in any letter case.
rules.reason: Every observed value is a size in ounces written with a unit suffix, such as '12.0 oz', '16.0 ounce' or '12.0 OZ.'. Anything else is a malformed size.

rules.condition: Alcohol by volume, stored as a fraction, must be between 0 and 0.2.
rules.reason: ABV is stored as a fraction; observed values run from 0.035 to 0.099. Craft beers rarely go above about 13% ABV. A value above 0.2 most likely means a percentage was entered as a whole number (e.g. 5.5), and negative values are impossible.

rules.condition: ABV must be a plain numeric value, without a '%' suffix or other text.
rules.reason: Some values arrive as strings like '0.08%', which combine a fraction value with a percent sign. That format is ambiguous and cannot be parsed reliably.

rules.condition: International Bitterness Units must be between 0 and 200.
rules.reason: Observed IBU runs from 4 to 120. Even extreme double IPAs stay below about 150, and negative values are impossible. The 200 limit leaves headroom for rare legitimate beers.
Style is never missing in the training sample and is a core descriptive attribute of each beer.
City is never missing in the training sample. Every brewery has a location.

rules.condition: When present, state must be a valid two-letter US state or DC postal code.
rules.reason: The dataset covers US craft breweries, and all observed values are two-letter US state codes. Only 48 of the codes have been seen so far, so all 51 are allowed to avoid flagging legitimate new states.
